nodes.description: A session handoff document, docs/handoffs/2026-08-05-step-4-testbench-migration.md, recording the migration of package tests to the shared package-testbench.

nodes.label: Private Messaging System
nodes.rationale: Direct user-to-user messaging with encrypted bodies, read receipts and policy-based access, delivered as both a Blade/Alpine web UI and a Sanctum-authenticated REST API.
nodes.description: The Private Messaging System, a feature providing user-to-user messaging with real-time notifications and API access, documented in docs/MESSAGING.md.

nodes.label: Message Model
nodes.rationale: Holds sender/recipient relations, between()/unread() scopes and markAsRead()/isRead(); keeps conversation querying in one place rather than in controllers.
nodes.description: The Message model documented in MESSAGING.md, backing the private messaging system's messages table and MessageController.

nodes.label: MessageController
nodes.rationale: Seven actions (index, show, store, markAsRead, destroy, users, unreadCount) that validate input, authorize via policy and handle encryption/decryption at the boundary.
nodes.description: MessageController, the controller handling private messaging requests, working with the Message model and MessagePolicy documented in the Messaging Architecture.

nodes.label: MessagePolicy
nodes.rationale: Laravel Policies chosen over ad-hoc checks: standard pattern, centralized logic, easy to test, and works with Blade directives and middleware. Users view messages they sent or received, update only what they sent, delete either side.
nodes.description: MessagePolicy, the authorization policy class governing who can view or act on messages in the Private Messaging System.

nodes.label: messages table schema
nodes.rationale: sender_id/recipient_id foreign keys with cascade delete, encrypted text body, nullable read_at.
nodes.description: The messages database table schema underlying the Private Messaging System, described in docs/MESSAGING.md.

nodes.label: Message encryption at rest
nodes.rationale: Laravel Crypt (AES-256-CBC) encrypts each message body individually. Chosen because it is built in, needs no extra infrastructure, and manages keys via APP_KEY. Per-message rather than per-column encryption allows selective decryption and least privilege. Trade-offs: encrypted messages cannot be searched without decrypting, and key rotation requires re-encrypting everything.
nodes.description: A design note in the messaging developer docs about encrypting stored message content at rest.

nodes.label: No conversations table
nodes.rationale: Messages are stored directly and conversations derived dynamically: simpler schema, fewer joins, fast direct-message queries. Trade-off: adding group messaging would require refactoring to a conversations table plus a participants pivot.
nodes.description: No conversations table documents that the messaging schema tracks conversations implicitly via the messages table rather than a dedicated table.

nodes.label: Conversation query indexes
nodes.rationale: Composite (sender_id, recipient_id) index optimizes the between() scope; a single recipient_id index optimizes unread-message queries used by the conversation list.
nodes.description: Database indexes on the messages table that optimize conversation queries, documented in the messaging developer notes.

nodes.label: Separate API (Sanctum) and web (session) routes
nodes.rationale: Keeps the web UI on session auth while exposing the same behaviour to token clients; enables future mobile app integration without reworking authentication.
nodes.description: Separate API (Sanctum) and web (session) routes describes the messaging system's dual authentication route split between token-based API access and session-based web access.

nodes.label: Alpine.js for the messaging UI
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Vue/React because it is lightweight, needs no build step for the MVP, integrates with Blade and matches the Livewire ecosystem. Migration to Livewire components is noted as a future option.
nodes.description: Alpine.js for the messaging UI documents the frontend framework choice for the private messaging web interface.

nodes.label: Layered authorization
nodes.rationale: Authorization is checked at routes (middleware), controller (policy) and views (Blade directives) so a single missed check cannot bypass access control.
nodes.description: A layered authorization approach for messaging, enforced via MessagePolicy, documented in the messaging developer notes.

nodes.label: @json() directive for JS contexts
nodes.rationale: Blade's @json() is used instead of raw {{ }} when embedding values into JavaScript, closing an XSS hole found in code review.
nodes.description: A documented XSS-prevention practice using Blade's @json() directive when embedding data into JavaScript in the messaging interface.

nodes.label: CSRF protection on state-changing requests
nodes.description: CSRF protection on state-changing requests documents the messaging web interface's use of Laravel's CSRF middleware for mutating requests.

nodes.label: Sanctum API authentication
nodes.description: Sanctum API authentication, used to secure the Messaging REST API endpoints as documented in docs/MESSAGING.md.

nodes.label: Messaging REST API endpoints
nodes.rationale: Seven endpoints: list conversations, conversation with user, send, mark read, delete, list users, unread count.
nodes.description: Messaging REST API endpoints are the Sanctum-authenticated HTTP routes documented in MESSAGING.md for the private messaging system.

nodes.label: Messaging web interface
nodes.rationale: Blade views (layout/index/show) with a conversation list, unread counts and a new-message modal.
nodes.description: The Alpine.js-driven web UI for the private messaging system, kept separate from the Sanctum-authenticated API and protected by CSRF on state-changing requests.

nodes.label: Messaging test suites
nodes.rationale: MessageTest covers model logic, relationships, scopes and encryption; MessageApiTest covers endpoints, authentication, authorization and validation.
nodes.description: Messaging test suites are the automated tests covering the private messaging system's architecture, referenced in MESSAGING_ARCHITECTURE.md.

nodes.label: Real-time notification system
nodes.rationale: Dual-channel delivery: every notification is persisted to the database for history and broadcast over websockets for immediacy, so reliability does not depend on the socket connection.
nodes.description: The real-time notification system, which delivers queued notifications over a Pusher broadcasting driver to private user broadcast channels.

nodes.label: Pusher broadcasting driver
nodes.description: Pusher broadcasting driver is the real-time notification transport documented as part of the notification system's broadcast services.

nodes.label: Alternative broadcast services
nodes.rationale: Ably, Laravel Reverb and Soketi are drop-in alternatives to Pusher, so the implementation avoids coupling to one vendor.
nodes.description: Documented alternative broadcasting drivers that can replace Pusher for real-time notifications.

nodes.label: Private user broadcast channels
nodes.rationale: App.Models.User.{id}, user.{userId} and notifications.{userId} are all private and require channel authorization, keeping notification payloads off public channels.
nodes.description: Private user broadcast channels, used by the real-time notification system together with the Laravel Echo client listener and MessagePolicy.

nodes.label: Queued notification delivery (ShouldQueue)
nodes.rationale: All notifications implement ShouldQueue so broadcasting and persistence happen off the request cycle.
nodes.description: The pattern of dispatching notifications like ActivityNotification, FriendRequestNotification, and NewMessageNotification asynchronously via Laravel's ShouldQueue interface.

nodes.label: NewMessageNotification
nodes.description: NewMessageNotification, a queued Laravel notification documented in NOTIFICATIONS.md that alerts users to new private messages.

nodes.label: FriendRequestNotification
nodes.description: FriendRequestNotification is a notification class documented in NOTIFICATIONS.md delivering queued friend-request alerts.

nodes.label: ActivityNotification
nodes.description: ActivityNotification is a notification class documented in NOTIFICATIONS.md that delivers activity alerts, part of the real-time notifications implementation.

nodes.label: notifications table
nodes.rationale: UUID primary key for distributed-system compatibility, polymorphic notifiable, JSON data column and read_at tracking.
nodes.description: The notifications database table underpinning the real-time notification system, described in the implementation summary.

nodes.label: Laravel Echo client listener
nodes.rationale: Initializes only when Pusher env vars are present, subscribes to the authenticated user channel and re-dispatches a notification-received custom event for the UI to consume.
nodes.description: A Laravel Echo client listener is the browser-side subscriber documented for real-time notification delivery over private user broadcast channels.

nodes.label: Browser push notifications
nodes.description: Documented browser push notification feature described in the real-time notifications documentation.

nodes.label: Advanced search across users, posts and groups
nodes.description: Advanced search across users, posts and groups is the feature covered by the Advanced Search Architecture and Functionality documentation.

nodes.label: SearchService
nodes.rationale: Service layer holding searchUsers/searchPosts/searchGroups/searchAll so filter-to-query translation is reusable and testable outside controllers.
nodes.description: SearchService, the search module's service class documented in SEARCH_FUNCTIONALITY.md that backs SearchController with eager loading, pagination limits and Group/Post model queries.

nodes.label: SearchController
nodes.rationale: Validates filters then delegates to SearchService; validation at the edge prevents malformed queries reaching the database.
nodes.description: SearchController is the HTTP controller documented in SEARCH_ARCHITECTURE.md that exposes the search API endpoints backed by SearchService.

nodes.label: Search API endpoints
nodes.rationale: /api/search/users, /posts, /groups and /all, each accepting query, entity filters, date ranges, ordering and per_page (1-100).
nodes.description: The search API endpoints documented in SEARCH_FUNCTIONALITY.md, served by SearchController and subject to search rate limiting.

nodes.label: Post model
nodes.rationale: belongsTo author, with published/status/byAuthor/dateRange/search scopes.
nodes.description: The Post model, an Eloquent model used to demonstrate full-text search functionality in docs/SEARCH_FUNCTIONALITY.md.

nodes.label: Group model
nodes.rationale: belongsTo owner, with type/byOwner/search scopes.
nodes.description: An Eloquent model used by the search functionality, referenced alongside reusable search scopes and SearchService in the search architecture docs.

nodes.label: Reusable Eloquent search scopes
nodes.rationale: scopeSearch on each model keeps search logic DRY and consistent instead of duplicating LIKE clauses in every controller.
nodes.description: Reusable Eloquent query scopes shared across models such as Group and Post to implement consistent, optimized search behavior.

nodes.label: Search database indexes
nodes.rationale: B-tree indexes on searchable and filterable columns (name, title, status, created_at, is_active) plus foreign keys; expected 50-80% reduction in query time on indexed columns.
nodes.description: The database indexes documented in SEARCH_OPTIMIZATION.md that speed up full-text and filtered search queries.

nodes.label: Full-text indexes
nodes.rationale: Groups carry a full-text index on name/description. Posts deliberately do not: they use plain B-tree indexes and LIKE matching via the search scope.
nodes.description: Full-text indexes on the Post model, part of the search performance optimizations documented alongside the search engine migration path.

nodes.label: Search API rate limiting
nodes.rationale: 60 requests per minute per IP protects against DoS and enforces fair resource distribution.
nodes.description: The rate limiting applied to search API endpoints, documented in SEARCH_OPTIMIZATION.md, to prevent abuse of search and translation lookups.

nodes.label: Selective column loading
nodes.rationale: Standalone search controllers select only needed columns (60-90% memory reduction). The shared SearchService does not yet do this and still returns full models.
nodes.description: Selective column loading is a SearchService performance optimization that limits queried columns, documented in Search Performance Optimization.

nodes.label: Eager loading to avoid N+1
nodes.description: Eager loading to avoid N+1, a search-optimization technique used by SearchService and documented in the Messaging Developer Notes and search architecture docs.

nodes.label: Enforced pagination limits
nodes.rationale: Default 15, maximum 100 records per page prevents memory exhaustion from unbounded result sets.
nodes.description: Enforced pagination limits, a search-optimization safeguard implemented in SearchService and documented in the search architecture and optimization docs.

nodes.label: modules/search package
nodes.rationale: The search code moved out of app/ into modules/search; the package README is the canonical reference.
nodes.description: The modules/search package documented in SEARCH_FUNCTIONALITY.md, providing the SearchService and search indexing capability.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/module-search-demo
nodes.rationale: Holds the demo-shaped Post and Group models that the search docs describe.
nodes.description: liberusoftware/module-search-demo, a demo liberu-module package illustrating the search module's Group and Post models and functionality.

nodes.label: Full-text search engine migration path
nodes.rationale: LIKE-based search suits small-to-medium datasets; Laravel Scout with Meilisearch/Algolia or Elasticsearch is the documented escape hatch for larger ones.
nodes.description: A documented future search migration path in SEARCH_FUNCTIONALITY.md describing a potential move to a dedicated full-text search engine.

nodes.label: liberu-module Composer package
nodes.rationale: Modules are independently versioned Composer packages installed into modules/{name}; Composer owns discovery and autoloading.
nodes.description: The liberu-module Composer package type used for domain packages under modules/, installed via the composer-installer plugin and described by a module.json manifest.

nodes.label: module.json manifest
nodes.rationale: Owns runtime metadata, provided/required capabilities, enablement defaults and Filament plugin declarations, separate from Composer's installation metadata.
nodes.description: The module.json manifest each liberu-module package carries, declaring its provider, capability declarations, module category and default enablement.

nodes.label: Capability declarations (provides / requires)
nodes.rationale: Dependencies are declared twice on purpose: Composer require controls installation and autoloading, manifest requires/required_capabilities control the enabled runtime graph.
nodes.description: The module.json manifest mechanism for declaring a module's provided and required capabilities, documented in MODULE_DEVELOPMENT.md.

nodes.label: Module categories
nodes.rationale: integration, domain, presentation or theme; framework presentation dependencies must stay out of domain packages.
nodes.description: Module categories classify modules (e.g. domain, presentation) as described in the Module Development Guide alongside the module.json manifest.

nodes.label: Explicit module enablement
nodes.rationale: Bundled packages default to disabled in their manifests and the application enables its composition explicitly, so installing a package never implies booting it.
nodes.description: Explicit module enablement, the rule that a module's installation does not imply it boots, requiring an explicit enablement decision per docs/MODULE_DEVELOPMENT.md.

nodes.label: Module manager (provider lifecycle authority)
nodes.rationale: The root application bootstraps only the module manager, which discovers installed liberu-module packages, validates the graph, orders providers by dependency and registers only enabled modules.
nodes.description: The module manager, described as the provider lifecycle authority in docs/MODULE_DEVELOPMENT.md, responsible for discovering, ordering and booting module providers.

nodes.label: No extra.laravel.providers auto-discovery
nodes.rationale: Runtime modules declare their provider in extra.liberu.provider and must not use Laravel's auto-discovery, because the module manager is the single provider lifecycle authority.
nodes.description: No extra.laravel.providers auto-discovery documents that module packages deliberately omit Laravel's auto-discovery so enablement stays an explicit host decision.

nodes.label: module:validate command
nodes.rationale: Checks that Liberu package dependencies are represented consistently, required versions are installed, providers are valid, capability providers are unambiguous and the enabled graph has no gaps or cycles.
nodes.description: The module:validate Artisan command documented in MODULE_DEVELOPMENT.md that checks module manifests and capability declarations for correctness.

nodes.label: No informal cross-module integration
nodes.rationale: A module must not query another module's tables or import its models as an integration API; use a contract, application service, event or documented schema extension instead.
nodes.description: A documented rule in the module development guide prohibiting informal cross-module table access, requiring contract packages instead.

nodes.label: Contract packages
nodes.rationale: Small shared-interface packages let adapters depend on a stable boundary without importing an implementation.
nodes.description: Contract packages are small Composer packages (e.g. analytics-contracts, localization-contracts) that define adapter interfaces for implementation independence between modules.

nodes.label: Companion *-filament presentation module
nodes.rationale: Filament code lives in a companion presentation package rather than its domain module, keeping domain packages presentation-agnostic.
nodes.description: A companion *-filament presentation module holds the Filament UI for a domain module, keeping the domain package presentation-agnostic.

nodes.label: filament_plugins manifest declaration
nodes.rationale: The presentation manifest names which panel (admin or app) receives its plugin class; plugin identifiers must be unique within a panel.
nodes.description: The filament_plugins manifest declaration is the module.json field naming a module's admin/app Filament plugin classes for ModulePlugins to instantiate.

nodes.label: App\Filament\ModulePlugins
nodes.rationale: Composes plugin instances from enabled manifests so panel providers never hard-code module plugins.
nodes.description: App\Filament\ModulePlugins, the host class documented in MODULE_DEVELOPMENT.md that composes Filament panel plugins from each enabled module's manifest declarations.

nodes.label: Admin Filament panel
nodes.rationale: Panel key 'admin' is for operational management surfaces.
nodes.description: The Admin Filament panel is the default tenant-scoped Filament panel composed from enabled modules' plugins, described in the Module Development Guide.

nodes.label: App Filament panel
nodes.rationale: Panel key 'app' is for tenant/user-facing functionality.
nodes.description: The /app Filament panel described in the module development guide, composed from enabled module plugins.

nodes.label: Package-owned tests
nodes.rationale: Every module carries its own tests under modules/{name}/tests, at minimum metadata tests verifying Composer/manifest agreement, dependencies and the provider.
nodes.description: Package-owned tests, the convention that each package ships and runs its own tests using liberusoftware/package-testbench rather than relying on the host.

nodes.label: Reproducible composition from the lockfile
nodes.rationale: Hidden filesystem-scanning conventions are avoided so Composer metadata, the manifest and explicit enablement are enough to reproduce the composition.
nodes.description: A documented principle that the host composition is reproducible from the Composer lockfile.

nodes.label: Module release workflow
nodes.rationale: Update the changelog, validate the graph, run focused and root suites, release from the package repository, then update the consuming application's constraint and lockfile.
nodes.description: The documented workflow in MODULE_DEVELOPMENT.md for releasing a module change, from validation through fleet-wide publishing.

nodes.label: liberu-theme Composer package
nodes.rationale: Themes are independent Composer packages installed into tracked /themes/{name} directories and own presentation only; business rules, authorization, queries and mutations stay in modules.
nodes.description: liberu-theme, the Composer package type for Liberu theme packages, installed via liberusoftware/composer-installer into the unified /themes root directory.

nodes.label: theme.json manifest
nodes.rationale: Declares name, label, version, provider, type, parent, colors and the declared asset entries.
nodes.description: The theme.json manifest a liberu-theme Composer package carries, declaring parent inheritance and driving Vite theme asset auto-discovery.

nodes.label: Theme parent inheritance chain
nodes.rationale: Child themes override only differing assets and inherit views/assets through a finite, validated parent chain; view lookup is child theme, parent chain, module default, then application fallback.
nodes.description: The parent-chain mechanism, walked by ThemeManager::inheritanceChain(), by which public themes like default, dark, and clear-signal fall back to the shared base theme.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-base
nodes.rationale: Shared root theme: accessible layout, semantic tokens, cascade layers and progressive JS primitives.
nodes.description: liberusoftware/theme-base, the root theme package defining semantic design tokens inherited by theme-clear-signal, theme-dark and theme-default.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-default
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-default package, a public theme in the theme architecture that inherits from theme-base.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-dark
nodes.rationale: Dark presentation achieved purely through token overrides on base.
nodes.description: liberusoftware/theme-dark is a public theme package documented in Theme Architecture, inheriting semantic design tokens from theme-base.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-clear-signal
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-clear-signal package, a public theme in the theme architecture that inherits from theme-base.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/composer-installer
nodes.rationale: Composer 2 plugin handling both liberu-theme and liberu-module: validates kebab-case installer names, rejects unsafe paths and collisions, and installs deterministically to /themes or /modules.
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/composer-installer Composer plugin, which installs liberu-module and liberu-theme packages into the tracked modules/ and themes/ directories.

nodes.label: Tracked installed package directories
nodes.rationale: Consuming applications commit both the lockfile and the reproduced /modules and /themes trees; root path repositories let Composer recognize the tracked source at the installer path instead of overwriting it.
nodes.description: The convention that modules/ and themes/ are Composer install targets that are also tracked in Git, so a fresh composer install can clobber tracked changes.

nodes.label: Theme selection precedence
nodes.rationale: Tenant-and-surface, then site-and-surface, then configured surface, then safe default. User/session preference may only select a discovered compatible theme; invalid selections warn and fall back.
nodes.description: The order of precedence documented in THEME_ARCHITECTURE.md by which the active theme is resolved (e.g. capability, site setting, config default).

nodes.label: theme:validate / theme:cache / theme:clear
nodes.description: theme:validate / theme:cache / theme:clear are Artisan commands for validating and managing the theme system's cache, documented in Theme Architecture and the Theme System Guide.

nodes.label: Semantic design tokens
nodes.rationale: Themes consume tokens for light, dark, contrast, state, focus, motion, spacing, typography, radius, elevation, borders, breakpoints and layering rather than hard-coded values.
nodes.description: Semantic design tokens, the shared styling variables defined by liberusoftware/theme-base and consumed by theme-dark and other child themes.

nodes.label: Theme accessibility requirements
nodes.rationale: WCAG 2.2 AA target verified with automated checks plus keyboard and screen-reader journeys; CSS honors reduced motion, forced colors and bidirectional layout; JS is progressive and CSP-safe.
nodes.description: Theme accessibility requirements are the accessibility standards themes must meet, documented alongside semantic design tokens in Theme Architecture.

nodes.label: Deterministic theme builds
nodes.rationale: Builds fail on missing manifest assets or unresolved imports; /public/build is deployment output while source assets remain in each package.
nodes.description: A documented principle that theme asset builds must be deterministic, tied to Vite's theme asset auto-discovery.

nodes.label: ThemeManager service
nodes.rationale: Discovers themes, resolves the active theme, exposes theme/view/asset paths and registers theme view paths with Laravel's view finder.
nodes.description: The ThemeManager service documented in the Theme Quick Reference, resolving theme parent inheritance and exposing theme helper functions and selection precedence.

nodes.label: ThemeServiceProvider
nodes.rationale: Registers the ThemeManager singleton, determines the active theme at boot, registers theme view paths and Blade directives, and shares theme data with views.
nodes.description: ThemeServiceProvider, the service provider that registers theme Blade directives, resolves the active theme and persists theme preference.

nodes.label: Theme helper functions
nodes.rationale: theme(), active_theme(), set_theme(), theme_asset(), theme_path(), theme_views_path(), theme_layout().
nodes.description: Blade/PHP helper functions documented in THEME_QUICK_REFERENCE.md for working with the theme system, such as resolving active theme assets.

nodes.label: Theme Blade directives
nodes.rationale: @themeCss, @themeJs, @themeAsset, @themeLayout and @themeVite; @themeVite selects declared built entries and falls back to the application bundle when unavailable.
nodes.description: Theme Blade directives, custom Blade syntax registered by ThemeServiceProvider for rendering theme-aware views.

nodes.label: Livewire theme switcher
nodes.description: The Livewire component that lets a user switch the active theme in the UI, documented in the theme visual overview.

nodes.label: Theme preference persistence
nodes.rationale: Authenticated users persist to users.theme_preference; guests fall back to session storage.
nodes.description: The mechanism for storing a user's or site's chosen theme so it persists across requests, coordinated with SetLocale middleware and ThemeServiceProvider.

nodes.label: Vite theme asset auto-discovery
nodes.rationale: vite.config.js reads every themes/*/theme.json and builds whatever assets.css and assets.js declare, so a consuming application needs no build change to add a theme.
nodes.description: Vite theme asset auto-discovery, the mechanism by which vite.config.js reads every theme.json to build CSS/JS entry points for the host's Vite pipeline.

nodes.label: Unified /themes root directory
nodes.rationale: Theme views, CSS and JS were consolidated from three split resources/ trees into one directory per theme, so a theme is added or removed as a single unit.
nodes.description: The unified /themes root directory that consolidates all theme packages under one tracked location in the host.

nodes.label: Theme release and upgrade flow
nodes.rationale: Release from the theme's own repository, update constraint and lockfile, reinstall, review the tracked /themes diff, validate, build and test. Conflicts are resolved by selecting a package version and reinstalling, never by hand-merging installed output; breaking manifest/token/slot changes need a major version.
nodes.description: The documented workflow in THEME_ARCHITECTURE.md for releasing and upgrading theme packages.

nodes.label: Multi-language support
nodes.rationale: English, Spanish, French and German out of the box, with automated machine translation and cached results.
nodes.description: The multi-language support feature documented in MULTI_LANGUAGE.md, covering locale resolution via SetLocale middleware and machine translation.

nodes.label: config('app.supported_locales')
nodes.description: config('app.supported_locales') lists the application's enabled locales (en/es/fr/de), used by the LanguageSwitcher and SetLocale middleware.

nodes.label: SetLocale middleware
nodes.rationale: Resolution order: locale query parameter, session value, authenticated user's preference, Accept-Language header, then the default locale.
nodes.description: SetLocale middleware, which resolves the active locale from request, session and user settings, documented in the Multi-Language Support guide.

nodes.label: TranslationService (MyMemory)
nodes.rationale: Wraps the free MyMemory API; can be swapped by binding a subclass in a service provider, which keeps callers independent of the translation vendor.
nodes.description: TranslationService (MyMemory), the localization-mymemory adapter providing on-demand machine translation, with caching and the translate:generate artisan command.

nodes.label: Translation caching
nodes.rationale: API translations are cached for 30 days to stay within MyMemory's free-tier rate limits and avoid repeat calls.
nodes.description: Translation caching stores machine-translation results to reduce repeated calls, documented alongside search API rate limiting and the MyMemory TranslationService.

nodes.label: translate:generate artisan command
nodes.description: An Artisan command documented in the multi-language support docs that generates translations via the MyMemory TranslationService.

nodes.label: LanguageSwitcher Livewire component
nodes.rationale: Lives in modules/localization-livewire and is mounted where a switcher is wanted.
nodes.description: LanguageSwitcher is a Livewire component in localization-core-livewire for switching the active locale, not yet mounted anywhere in the application.

nodes.label: Localization module split
nodes.rationale: The localization code moved out of app/ into modules/localization, modules/localization-livewire and modules/localization-mymemory; each package README is canonical.
nodes.description: The localization module split divides localization functionality across several liberu-module Composer packages, per Multi-Language Support Documentation.

nodes.label: Tabbed user form
nodes.rationale: Basic Info / Roles & Permissions / Account Settings tabs reduce cognitive load on a long form; password is required on create and optional on edit.
nodes.description: A tabbed layout added to the admin user-management form, documented in IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md.

nodes.label: Users table filters and badges
nodes.rationale: Role multi-select, email verified, email unverified and recently-joined filters, with role and team count badges for fast visual scanning.
nodes.description: Users table filters and badges are Filament table UI features for the admin user-management enhancement, documented in the Quick Reference Guide.

nodes.label: Admin dashboard widgets
nodes.rationale: UserStatsOverview, LatestUsersWidget and UsersByRoleChart give an at-a-glance view of the user base.
nodes.description: Admin dashboard widgets are Filament panel widgets covered in the Implementation Summary as part of the admin user-management enhancement.

nodes.label: Filament Shield role-based access
nodes.rationale: Roles and permissions are managed through Shield on top of Spatie Permission, with team-scoped permissions; no new tables were needed.
nodes.description: Filament Shield role-based access, the authorization mechanism gating admin panel user-management features, documented in the Implementation Summary and Quick Reference guide.

nodes.label: Password auto-hashing on save
nodes.description: Password auto-hashing on save documents that the user model's password attribute is automatically hashed when saved, noted in the admin panel implementation summary.

nodes.label: Single-context domain docs
nodes.rationale: One root CONTEXT.md glossary and one docs/adr/ directory cover the host plus every modules/ and themes/ package; switch to CONTEXT-MAP.md with per-package contexts only if module vocabularies actually diverge.
nodes.description: The domain.md convention that domain documentation for the host and all modules/themes lives in a single root CONTEXT.md and one docs/adr/ directory rather than being scattered per package.

nodes.label: CONTEXT.md glossary
nodes.rationale: Output naming a domain concept must use the glossary's term; a missing term is a signal of either invented language or a real gap.
nodes.description: The root CONTEXT.md glossary document described in the agent domain docs convention.

nodes.label: docs/adr/ decision records
nodes.rationale: Output contradicting an existing ADR must surface the conflict explicitly rather than silently overriding it.
nodes.description: The docs/adr/ directory holding the repository's architecture decision records.

nodes.label: GitHub Issues as the issue tracker
nodes.rationale: All issue and PRD operations go through the gh CLI, with the repo inferred from git remote.
nodes.description: GitHub Issues on liberusoftware/boilerplate-laravel is the canonical issue tracker, driven by the gh CLI per docs/agents/issue-tracker.md.

nodes.label: PRs-as-request-surface flag
nodes.rationale: Currently 'no'. GitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare #42 must be resolved by trying gh pr view then gh issue view.
nodes.description: A documented flag in the issue-tracker convention marking pull requests as a request surface for triage.

nodes.label: Wayfinder map and child tickets
nodes.rationale: A single wayfinder:map issue holds Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog; child tickets are sub-issues, and blocking uses GitHub's native issue dependencies keyed on the blocker's numeric database id.
nodes.description: The Wayfinder map and child tickets is a GitHub issue structure (rooted at issue #612) used to organize and track related work items in the issue tracker.

nodes.label: Canonical triage labels
nodes.rationale: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix — each label string equals its canonical role name in this repo.
nodes.description: Canonical triage labels are the standard GitHub issue labels used for triage, defined in docs/agents/triage-labels.md.

nodes.label: docs/CONFORMANCE.md
nodes.rationale: The conformance deliverable: scope, every decision with its enforcement mechanism, the defect register, and the step -1 to 9 migration sequence with gates and rollback. Later step blocks correct earlier prose in the same document.
nodes.description: docs/CONFORMANCE.md, the specification document describing the host's conformance requirements and zero-diff gate for module packages.

nodes.label: Wayfinder map issue #612
nodes.rationale: Closed at 15/15 tickets; its destination was a spec and no production code changed. A fresh effort means a fresh map, not reopening it.
nodes.description: GitHub issue #612, the 'Wayfinder map' tracking issue referenced in a conformance handoff for coordinating child conformance tickets.

nodes.label: liberusoftware vs liberu vendor prefix
nodes.rationale: The vendor was taken as liberu/* early then reversed by the owner back to liberusoftware/*. This puts the repo in deliberate disagreement with liberusoftware/documentation, which mandates liberu/* — a documentation PR is owed.
nodes.description: A recorded decision in a conformance-map handoff weighing 'liberusoftware' against 'liberu' as the Composer vendor prefix.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/package-testbench
nodes.rationale: Shared test harness every package dev-requires; version 1.2.0 implements all seven boundary rules that were being kept in the host, making their deletion safe.
nodes.description: liberusoftware/package-testbench, the shared Composer package that supplies boundary test suites, Pint and PHPStan configuration used by every module package.

nodes.label: scripts/migrate-testbench
nodes.rationale: Idempotent fleet migration script, piloted on analytics-core and reverted, moved out of the scratchpad because WSL wipes /tmp on restart.
nodes.description: scripts/migrate-testbench is a script documented in a handoff for migrating packages to use liberusoftware/package-testbench.

nodes.label: Packagist namespace registration blocker
nodes.rationale: Nine packages 404 on Packagist, blocking the fleet migration because each package must resolve package-testbench standalone. The fallback is a per-package repositories vcs entry, which unblocks immediately at the cost of a later cleanup release wave.
nodes.description: The Packagist namespace registration blocker is an obstacle noted in a handoff that delayed publishing liberusoftware/package-testbench to Packagist.

nodes.label: modules/ is Composer output
nodes.rationale: vendor/composer/installed.json owns the autoload map and is written from each package's published composer.json, so a rename makes the host unbootable until the wave is published. The gate for a rename is each package's own suite, never the host's.
nodes.description: The documented fact, recorded in a conformance handoff, that the modules/ directory is Composer install output for tracked packages rather than hand-edited source.

nodes.label: Root composer install clobbers tracked packages
nodes.rationale: A root install reinstalls every package from Packagist over the tracked /modules and /themes files. git checkout alone does not recover it — untracked files the published packages brought in survive and can be committed as if they were real work.
nodes.description: Root composer install clobbers tracked packages documents a pitfall where running composer install at the root overwrites the tracked modules/themes directories.

nodes.label: Publishing mirrors all packages, not just changed ones
nodes.rationale: Sweeping only changed packages let three stale packages and one regression reach GitHub; the whole fleet must be swept.
nodes.description: The documented rule, recorded in a conformance handoff, that publishing mirrors every package in the fleet rather than only the ones that changed.

nodes.label: composer.json version fields are load-bearing
nodes.rationale: ModuleValidator compares each manifest against Composer\InstalledVersions, so a bumped manifest fails the boot until the package is published, tagged and composer update'd — expect a red host in between.
nodes.description: composer.json version fields are load-bearing documents that a package's declared version drives tooling behavior and must not be treated as cosmetic, per a migration handoff.

nodes.label: A tag whose commit predates a fix
nodes.rationale: Composer resolves the tag, not main, so a stale tag is worse than no tag; bumping and re-tagging closed the gate.
nodes.description: Uma tag publicada cujo commit é anterior a uma correção, documentada no handoff de migração do testbench.

nodes.label: Host architecture boundary rules
nodes.rationale: ModuleBoundariesTest held 15 rules; seven moved to the testbench and the survivors are the whole-graph ones — theme parents resolving, Composer owning every autoload boundary, cross-package namespace dependencies, one Composer vendor, and the two enablement rules.
nodes.description: The set of executable architecture rules that assert module boundaries (enablement, provider discovery, theme inheritance) across the whole host codebase.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/.github reusable workflows
nodes.rationale: Three reusable workflows so every repository gets real CI without carrying a copy of the workflow body.
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/.github repository providing reusable GitHub Actions workflows consumed by each package's CI.

nodes.label: Handoffs live in docs/handoffs/
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md overrides the /handoff skill's temp-directory default because WSL wipes /tmp exactly when the next session needs the document.
nodes.description: The documented rule that session handoff documents belong in docs/handoffs/, not a temp directory.

nodes.label: Missing config.allow-plugins across packages
nodes.rationale: 0 of 48 packages declared config.allow-plugins, so composer update fails inside every package because pestphp/pest-plugin is blocked; --no-plugins is a measurement workaround, not the fix.
nodes.description: A documented conformance defect where packages were missing the config.allow-plugins Composer setting.

nodes.label: Verify before asserting
nodes.rationale: Several confident claims were wrong on inspection: a CI gate of --min=83 measuring 5.6%, twelve architecture rules of which two never worked, and 'standalone-testable' packages that could not install standalone.
nodes.description: A documented principle to verify claims against the host's actual architecture rules before asserting them.

nodes.label: Packagist token stays out of the session
nodes.rationale: The token was never shared or stored; it belongs in ~/.config/composer/auth.json or a GitHub Actions secret, never in a repo or a chat transcript.
nodes.description: A documented security practice that the Packagist publishing token is kept out of the agent session.

nodes.label: Handoff: Conformance Step 5 (Test Redistribution)
nodes.rationale: Written so the next session does not re-derive state: it points at CONFORMANCE.md, the git log and CLAUDE.md rather than restating them, and records only environment state, traps and next steps.
nodes.description: A session handoff document, docs/handoffs/2026-08-06-step-5-test-redistribution.md, recording conformance step 5 which redistributed tests across packages.

nodes.label: Handoff: Conformance Step 4 (Testbench Migration)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by the step 5 handoff: its blocker is gone and its next-steps are done.
nodes.description: A session handoff document recording the state and next steps of the conformance effort's Step 4 testbench migration.

nodes.label: Conformance Step 5 — Test Redistribution
nodes.rationale: Tests move out of the host into the package that owns them; a test belongs in a package only if it needs nothing from the host. Moved so far: settings (3 tests), localization-core (locale middleware), localization-core-livewire (language switcher).
nodes.description: Conformance Step 5, documented in a dated handoff, covering the redistribution of tests out of the host and into their owning packages.

nodes.label: docs/CONFORMANCE.md — Conformance Plan
nodes.rationale: Its "Step N is done" blocks state what was actually found, including where the plan was wrong — the plan is corrected in writing rather than silently.
nodes.description: docs/CONFORMANCE.md, the conformance plan document referenced by conformance step handoffs.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/package-testbench
nodes.rationale: Shared boundary suites and test bootstrap so a new boundary rule is one testbench release rather than a 44-repository sweep. Version 1.7.0 at the time of this handoff.
nodes.description: liberusoftware/package-testbench, referenced in the test-redistribution handoff as the shared testing foundation for Liberu Developer Experience and other packages.

nodes.label: Trap: an empty tests/ directory does not publish
nodes.rationale: 34 packages shipped 1.2.0 with no tests/ at all; Pest aborts with 'The test directory [tests] does not exist'. The 44-package sweep passed only because the directory was still on disk locally. Fixed with a tracked tests/.gitkeep. Lesson: a fleet sweep does not prove what the tarball contains — only a reinstall does. Second occurrence of this class of error.
nodes.description: A documented pitfall noting that Git does not track an empty tests/ directory, so a package can publish without shipping any tests unless a placeholder file exists.

nodes.label: Trap: do not tag before something has run the shipped artifact
nodes.rationale: testbench 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 were tagged with a boundary suite that could not load. A tag is what Packagist publishes, so it is not recoverable the way a push is.
nodes.description: A documented pitfall warning not to tag a package release before something has actually exercised the shipped test artifact.

nodes.label: Trap: defineEnvironment() overrides must call parent
nodes.rationale: A package overriding defineEnvironment() without parent::defineEnvironment($app) loses the application key PackageTestCase sets (testbench 1.7.0).
nodes.description: Trap: defineEnvironment() overrides must call parent is a documented pitfall in the Conformance Step 5 handoff warning that package-testbench's defineEnvironment() overrides must call the parent implementation.

nodes.label: Trap: host goes red between a manifest bump and composer update
nodes.rationale: ModuleValidator compares the manifest against InstalledVersions, so the window between the two is expected red, not a fault.
nodes.description: A documented pitfall in the 2026-08-06 step-5 handoff describing how the host's tests can go red in the window between bumping a module manifest version and running composer update.

nodes.label: Trap: WSL DNS drops under parallel Composer
nodes.rationale: Sweep at -P 2 and retry; higher parallelism loses name resolution.
nodes.description: A documented pitfall in the 2026-08-06 step-5 handoff describing DNS resolution failures under WSL when running Composer operations in parallel.

nodes.label: Task #8 — searcher registry in search / search-demo split
nodes.rationale: Moving SearchService::searchPosts()/searchGroups() and two search-api controller actions into search-demo is a three-package refactor, not a move: searchAll() aggregates over types, so the honest design is a searcher registry in `search` that `search-demo` registers into — which is exactly what CONFORMANCE §3.4 objected to being hardcoded. search's own tests follow the code, not the other way round.
nodes.description: Task #8 from the 2026-08-06 step-5 test-redistribution handoff, tracking the split of the searcher registry between the search and search-demo modules.

nodes.label: Task #9 — adopt preserved messaging and blog tests
nodes.rationale: Tests preserved at commit 33550079 need adopting into their own repositories.
nodes.description: Task #9 from the 2026-08-06 step-5 test-redistribution handoff, tracking adoption of preserved messaging and blog tests.

nodes.label: Blocker: theme discovery is not Composer-driven
nodes.rationale: ThemeManager* and ThemeSwitcherTest need installed themes, but discovery reads base_path('themes') rather than InstalledVersions the way ModuleDiscovery does, and Testbench's base path is its own skeleton. Fixing it also closes the theme-support §4 row, where three successive guards had to be loosened to make the package bootable.
nodes.description: A documented blocker noting that theme discovery was not yet Composer-driven, recorded in the Conformance Step 5 test-redistribution handoff.

nodes.label: Risk: package CI has not been observed green
nodes.rationale: Runs on liberusoftware/module-* queued over an hour; every suite passes locally with the same command CI runs, but nobody has seen the workflows themselves pass since the migration. Check before assuming.
nodes.description: Documented risk in docs/handoffs/2026-08-06-step-5-test-redistribution.md that a package's CI pipeline has never been observed passing end-to-end.

nodes.label: Working agreement: verify before asserting
nodes.rationale: Mutation-test a new rule; outward-facing steps get confirmed; the plan is corrected in writing when wrong; no Claude attribution footers.
nodes.description: A working agreement recorded in the 2026-08-06 step-5 test-redistribution handoff to verify facts before asserting them.

nodes.label: Standalone Package Test Suite
nodes.rationale: Every package ships its own tests, run from a compatible host checkout as `vendor/bin/pest modules/<name>/tests`; changes must preserve the manifest, provider integration, package boundaries and declared PHP/Laravel compatibility.
nodes.description: The convention that each liberu-module package carries its own test suite runnable independently of the host, as with the Localization and Module Manager modules.

nodes.label: Team-Scoped Boundary
nodes.rationale: Real-estate transports and domain records are scoped to a team and pass explicit team context at every mutation boundary; unauthorized cross-team access surfaces as 403 Forbidden rather than a silently filtered result.
nodes.description: The Team-Scoped Boundary documented in the real-estate-core module, describing how core, API, Filament, and Livewire real estate packages relate under tenant/team scoping.

nodes.label: Presentation-Neutral Core Package
nodes.rationale: A domain core package owns rules and persistence but no UI, so Filament, Livewire and API adapters can be added, swapped or omitted without touching domain behaviour.
nodes.description: The Presentation-Neutral Core Package describes the real-estate-core module's design principle of keeping domain logic free of any specific UI framework, decoupled from Filament/Livewire presentation packages.

nodes.label: Adapter Over One Matching Core Package
nodes.rationale: Each -api, -filament and -livewire package adapts exactly one matching core package: it validates and authorizes at the boundary and delegates mutations to the core rather than reimplementing them.
nodes.description: The architecture principle that Livewire packages act as thin adapters over a single matching core domain package rather than duplicating domain logic.

nodes.label: Unprefixed Composer Name vs module- GitHub Repository
nodes.rationale: The published Composer/Packagist name drops the `module-` prefix carried by the GitHub source repository, so liberusoftware/real-estate-instructions on Composer is module-real-estate-instructions on GitHub.
nodes.description: The naming convention documented for real-estate-instructions whereby the Composer package name omits the module- prefix carried by its GitHub repository.

nodes.label: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme
nodes.description: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme, an OpenAPI security scheme in the real-estate-core API spec describing bearer-token authentication via Laravel Sanctum.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key Header
nodes.rationale: Replays a completed mutation for the same team, key and request body (8-255 chars), so a retried POST/PATCH/DELETE cannot double-apply; a mismatch returns 409 Conflict.
nodes.description: An HTTP header documented in the real estate API OpenAPI specs used to make write requests, such as offer transitions, safely retryable without duplicate side effects.

nodes.label: PaginationMeta Schema
nodes.description: PaginationMeta Schema, an OpenAPI component in the real-estate-core API spec describing pagination metadata shared across Real Estate API responses.

nodes.label: API Error Schema
nodes.description: API Error Schema, the shared OpenAPI schema defining the error response shape used across the real estate core and related API specifications.

nodes.label: 429 RateLimited Response
nodes.rationale: Every instructions operation declares a 429 response carrying a Retry-After header, making rate limiting part of the published contract rather than an undocumented gateway behaviour.
nodes.description: The 429 RateLimited response documented in the real-estate-instructions OpenAPI spec, returned when a client exceeds the API rate limit.

nodes.label: Provider-Neutral Domain, Replaceable Adapters

nodes.label: Sales Progression API v1 OpenAPI Spec
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI 3.1.0 contract for /api/v1/real-estate/sales-progressions; DELETE archives rather than deletes.
nodes.description: The OpenAPI v1 specification for the Real Estate Sales Progression API.

nodes.label: Valuations API v1 OpenAPI Spec
nodes.rationale: OpenAPI 3.1.0 contract for /api/v1/real-estate/valuations, including the workflow sub-resources schedule, complete, convert and comparables.

nodes.description: The OpenAPI v1 specification for the Real Estate Viewings API, including viewing lifecycle transitions.

nodes.label: Core/API/Filament/Livewire Package Split
nodes.rationale: Each real-estate domain ships as up to four independently published packages: a presentation-neutral core plus -api, -filament and -livewire adapters. Independence means a consumer installs only the surfaces it needs.
nodes.description: The Core/API/Filament/Livewire package split, a recurring architecture pattern where a real estate domain module is divided into a framework-neutral core plus separate API, Filament and Livewire presentation adapters.

nodes.label: Unprefixed Composer Name vs module- GitHub Repo
nodes.rationale: The Composer/Packagist package name drops the module- prefix that the GitHub source repository carries, so the same package is addressed by two different names depending on which system is naming it.
nodes.description: The naming convention documented for real-estate-property-management whereby a package's Composer name omits the module- prefix carried by its GitHub repository.

nodes.label: No App\ Namespace Dependency
nodes.rationale: A module never assumes application App\ classes exist, so it can be installed standalone and tested without the host.
nodes.description: A documented rule that the real-estate-properties module's domain code has no dependency on the host's App\ namespace.

nodes.label: Migration Owns Only the Package's Tables
nodes.rationale: A module's migration creates only the tables that package owns, and disabling the module does not delete data — enablement is a boot decision, not a data lifecycle decision.
nodes.description: A documented rule that each module's migrations only create or modify tables owned by that package.

nodes.label: Immutable Property History Entries
nodes.rationale: Property changes are recorded as immutable history entries rather than in-place edits, preserving an audit trail of lifecycle status changes.
nodes.description: A documented design in the real-estate-properties module where property history entries are immutable and preserved via archiving rather than hard deletion.

nodes.label: Replaceable Integration Services
nodes.rationale: Provider credentials and transport live in replaceable integration services outside the sync core, so a portal provider can be swapped without touching domain records.
nodes.description: A documented design principle in the real-estate-rightmove module that external integration services are replaceable behind an interface.

nodes.label: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme
nodes.rationale: Every real-estate API spec declares a single securitySchemes entry: http bearer with bearerFormat Sanctum, applied document-wide via top-level security.
nodes.description: The Sanctum bearer-token security scheme defined in the real estate valuations API's OpenAPI spec for authenticating API requests.

nodes.label: Shared Error Schema
nodes.rationale: Identical Error component in every spec: required message, plus optional code and a free-form errors object.
nodes.description: A shared OpenAPI schema, defined in the real estate valuations API spec, used to represent error responses consistently across the real-estate API specs.

nodes.label: Shared PaginationMeta Schema
nodes.rationale: Identical PaginationMeta component in every spec: current_page, per_page, total and last_page all required.
nodes.description: A shared OpenAPI schema, defined in the real estate valuations API spec, used to represent pagination metadata consistently across the real-estate API specs.

nodes.label: OpenAPI 3.1.0 Versioned API Contract
nodes.rationale: Each -api package ships its contract under openapi/v1/, matching the /api/v1/ route prefix, so an API version is a directory of the adapter rather than a branch of the domain.
nodes.description: The convention, documented across the real-estate API OpenAPI specs, that each real-estate API is published as a versioned OpenAPI 3.1.0 contract.

nodes.label: Archive Instead of Hard Delete
nodes.rationale: Rightmove and sales-progression DELETE endpoints return 204 described as 'Archived', preserving records rather than destroying them; the valuations and viewings specs describe the same verb as 'Deleted', so the convention is not uniform across the fleet.
nodes.description: A documented convention in the Rightmove Sync API spec that records are archived rather than hard-deleted, preserving history alongside immutable property history entries.

nodes.label: Valuation Workflow Transitions
nodes.rationale: Valuation state changes are POST sub-resources (schedule, complete, convert, comparables) rather than PATCH field writes, so each transition is an explicit named operation with its own authorization.
nodes.description: The set of allowed status transitions for a valuation record, defined in the real estate valuations API's OpenAPI spec.

nodes.label: Viewing Lifecycle Transitions
nodes.rationale: Viewing state changes are POST sub-resources (confirm, complete, cancel, no-show) rather than PATCH field writes, making each lifecycle move a distinct named operation.
nodes.description: The set of lifecycle status transitions for viewings documented in the Viewings API v1 OpenAPI spec.

nodes.label: Rightmove Sync Operation
nodes.rationale: Synchronizing a listing is a POST on the sync record itself (real.estate.rightmove.sync), colliding on the same path as the GET/PATCH/DELETE record operations.
nodes.description: An OpenAPI-documented operation in the Rightmove Sync API v1 spec that triggers synchronization with the Rightmove portal.

nodes.description: The domain specification section of the Real Estate Property Management module's README.

nodes.label: Property Management API Specification
nodes.description: The API specification section of the Real Estate Property Management module's README.

nodes.label: Property Management Livewire Specification
nodes.description: The Livewire specification section of the Real Estate Property Management module's README.

nodes.label: Capability Boundary Integration
nodes.rationale: Hosts integrate a package through its declared capabilities and public contracts rather than application-specific classes; consumers must not couple to internal tables or classes.
nodes.description: Documented concept in the roles-permissions module README describing the capability boundary integration between installation and enablement.

nodes.label: Category: foundation
nodes.rationale: Foundation-category packages are presentation-neutral domain cores.
nodes.description: A module category tag grouping foundational modules such as roles-permissions, scheduler-and-queues, search, sessions-and-devices, settings and two-factor-authentication.

nodes.label: Category: presentation
nodes.rationale: Presentation-category packages carry Filament, Livewire or HTTP-API surfaces so domain cores stay UI-agnostic.
nodes.description: Category: presentation, a classification tag grouping presentation-layer modules such as authorization-filament, search-api, sessions-and-devices-administration, settings-administration and theme-support-livewire.

nodes.label: Packagist Names Omit the module- Prefix
nodes.rationale: Source repositories use the `module-` GitHub prefix; Composer and Packagist package names intentionally omit it, so `liberusoftware/module-search` on GitHub is `liberusoftware/search` on Packagist.
nodes.description: A documented naming convention where Packagist package names drop the module- prefix used in the corresponding GitHub repository names.

nodes.label: Tracked modules/ Directory with Composer as Version Truth
nodes.rationale: The installed directory stays tracked by the host repository so the composition is reproducible from Git, while Composer and its lock file remain the authority on versions.
nodes.description: Tracked modules/ Directory with Composer as Version Truth describes the convention that the modules/ directory is Git-tracked while Composer remains the authoritative source for package versions.

nodes.label: Private Security Disclosure Policy
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities go to security@liberusoftware.com rather than public GitHub issues so a report can be handled before disclosure.
nodes.description: Private Security Disclosure Policy, documentation in the webhooks module README describing how to privately report security vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: Shared users Table
nodes.rationale: No package owns the users table; several packages extend it with their own migrations, which is the one place where the per-package persistence boundary is deliberately shared.
nodes.description: The shared users database table that the search module reads for permission checks, owned by the host application.

nodes.label: Sanctum Bearer Security Scheme
nodes.rationale: Every versioned API adapter declares a single global `sanctum` HTTP bearer scheme so authentication is uniform across the fleet's OpenAPI contracts.
nodes.description: The Sanctum bearer token security scheme documented in the real-estate-zoopla OpenAPI spec, used to authenticate API requests.

nodes.label: Versioned openapi/v1 Adapter Contract
nodes.rationale: Each -api module carries its own OpenAPI 3.1 document under openapi/v1/, so the HTTP contract is versioned independently of the domain package it adapts.
nodes.description: Versioned openapi/v1 Adapter Contract, the OpenAPI specification defining the stable versioned API contract for the real-estate-zoopla-api adapter.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla
nodes.rationale: Independent, team-scoped Zoopla synchronization core. It deliberately does not depend on the portal-reporting module; provider credentials and transport belong in replaceable integration services so the core stays free of vendor coupling.
nodes.description: The Real Estate Zoopla module, providing integration with the Zoopla property portal, split across core/API/Filament/Livewire packages.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla API
nodes.rationale: Independent versioned API adapter for Zoopla sync records, kept separate from the domain core.
nodes.description: Real Estate Zoopla API, the API-tier module exposing the real-estate-zoopla domain module's Zoopla portal sync functionality over HTTP.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla Filament
nodes.rationale: Independent Filament 5 adapter, so the Zoopla domain core ships no admin UI of its own.
nodes.description: The Filament admin UI adapter package for the Real Estate Zoopla module.

nodes.label: Real Estate Zoopla Livewire

nodes.description: The Livewire front-end adapter package for the Real Estate Zoopla module.

nodes.label: Liberu Authorization Filament
nodes.rationale: Filament role and permission management is a separate presentation package so the authorization core carries no Filament dependency.
nodes.description: Liberu Authorization Filament, a presentation-tier package wrapping Filament Shield to provide the roles-permissions capability's Filament UI over liberusoftware/roles-permissions.

nodes.label: Liberu Scheduler and Queues
nodes.rationale: Centralises unique/idempotent job policy, schedules, locks, retries, failures, monitoring and graceful deployment conventions so each module does not re-derive them.
nodes.description: Liberu Scheduler and Queues, the module providing the foundation.scheduler-queues capability for scheduled and queued task execution.

nodes.label: Liberu Search
nodes.rationale: Authorized search queries, filters, pagination and replaceable model configuration; model configuration is replaceable so the search core does not hardcode the host's searchable models.
nodes.description: Liberu Search, the module providing the foundation.search capability, with an accompanying Search API package.

nodes.label: Liberu Search API
nodes.rationale: Authenticated, rate-limited HTTP endpoints kept in a presentation package so the search core stays transport-agnostic.
nodes.description: The Liberu Search API package, a presentation-category module exposing the foundation.search.api capability.

nodes.label: Liberu Sessions and Devices
nodes.rationale: Privacy-conscious active-session inventory with current-session protection, so revoking sessions cannot lock the acting user out of their own session.
nodes.description: Liberu Sessions and Devices, a foundation-category liberu-module package that provides session/device management under the identity.sessions capability.

nodes.label: Liberu Sessions and Devices Administration
nodes.rationale: Accessible account security and preferences surface targeted at the app panel rather than the admin panel.
nodes.description: Liberu Sessions and Devices Administration is the Filament presentation package (foundation.sessions-devices capability) providing the admin UI for the Liberu Sessions and Devices module.

nodes.label: Liberu Settings
nodes.rationale: Typed application, organization, team/site and user settings with validation and deterministic cache invalidation — determinism matters because settings are read on every request path.
nodes.description: Liberu Settings, the module providing the foundation.settings capability for site-wide configuration management.

nodes.label: Liberu Settings Administration
nodes.rationale: Optional Filament settings administration surface; optional so a headless composition can consume settings without Filament.
nodes.description: Liberu Settings Administration, a presentation-category liberu-module package providing the Filament UI for the Liberu Settings module, built on filament/spatie-laravel-settings-plugin.

nodes.label: Liberu Theme Support
nodes.rationale: Theme discovery, view overrides, safe asset directives, preferences and panel palettes. Asset directives are 'safe' because themes are third-party packages whose declared assets must be validated before rendering.
nodes.description: Liberu Theme Support, the module providing the foundation.theme-support capability for theme configuration and asset resolution.

nodes.label: Liberu Theme Support Livewire

nodes.description: Liberu Theme Support Livewire é o pacote de apresentação (capability foundation.theme-support) baseado em Livewire 4 que oferece componentes de suporte ao gerenciamento de temas.

nodes.label: Liberu Two-Factor Authentication
nodes.rationale: TOTP enforcement, trusted-device policy and single-use recovery primitives; recovery codes are single-use so a leaked code cannot be replayed.
nodes.description: Liberu Two-Factor Authentication, a foundation-category liberu-module package providing TOTP-based two-factor auth under the identity.two-factor capability.

nodes.label: Liberu Webhooks
nodes.rationale: Endpoint registration, signing, filtering, delivery evidence, backoff, rotation, replay and logs. Delivery evidence and replay exist so an undelivered event is provable and recoverable rather than silently lost.
nodes.description: Liberu Webhooks, the module providing the foundation.webhooks capability for registering and dispatching outbound webhooks.

nodes.rationale: Composes the Liberu boilerplate foundation with project-relevant Real Estate core, API, Filament and Livewire modules. Foundation packages stay reusable and presentation-neutral; Real Estate packages are selected one-to-one across the four implementation indexes. Deferred frontend indexes are out of scope for this run.
nodes.description: Liberu Application Composition, documented in projects/LIBERU.md, describing how the host composes core/API/Filament/Livewire implementation packages.

nodes.label: Liberu Platform Scope
nodes.rationale: Cross-product Liberu modules are added to this scope only when not already owned by the application foundation or a product scope, preventing duplicate ownership of a capability.
nodes.description: Documentation describing the scope of the Liberu platform, indexing its application, API and core module areas.

nodes.label: Liberu API Modules Scope
nodes.rationale: Shared API access, webhooks, integrations, import/export and readiness contracts come from foundation packages; product APIs remain under their owning project scope.
nodes.description: Documentation describing the scope of API modules within the Liberu platform.

nodes.label: Liberu Core Modules Scope
nodes.rationale: Names the foundation core packages the current application consumes: application, identity, organizations and teams, settings, audit, search, notifications, files and media, observability, scheduler and queues, and supporting contracts.
nodes.description: The documented scope of core Liberu packages (identity, organizations-teams, scheduler-queues, search, settings) that form the foundation platform layer.

nodes.label: Four Implementation Indexes (core / api / filament / livewire)
nodes.rationale: Every product domain is published as a one-to-one set of four packages — domain core plus API, Filament and Livewire adapters — so presentation choice never forces a domain dependency.
nodes.description: Four Implementation Indexes (core / api / filament / livewire), the documented index structure in projects/LIBERU.md organizing each domain module by its adapter tier.

nodes.label: Liberu Real Estate scope
nodes.rationale: The scope covers agency operations end to end (properties, parties, listings, viewings, offers, progression, lettings, management, marketing, portal reporting) so that each capability is a separately releasable boundary rather than one monolithic estate-agency application.
nodes.description: The documented scope of the Liberu Real Estate project, defined in projects/real-estate/REAL-ESTATE.md, covering capabilities such as instructions, lettings, listings, marketing, matching, and media/documents.

nodes.label: Framework-neutral core boundary
nodes.rationale: Each capability has exactly one core boundary that carries no presentation framework, so the domain can be consumed by API, Filament or Livewire adapters interchangeably and the same rules hold whichever surface is installed.
nodes.description: The architectural boundary in the Real Estate project separating the framework-neutral domain core from its Filament, Livewire, and API adapter tiers.

nodes.label: One-to-one adapter rule
nodes.rationale: Adapters are optional and map one-to-one onto a core package, so a surface can be added or dropped without touching the domain and no adapter accumulates behaviour for more than one capability.
nodes.description: The one-to-one adapter rule requires each Real Estate domain module to have exactly one adapter package per presentation tier (API, Filament, Livewire).

nodes.label: API adapter tier
nodes.description: The API adapter tier of the Real Estate project, exposing the framework-neutral core through HTTP API modules.

nodes.label: Filament adapter tier
nodes.description: The Filament adapter tier of the Real Estate project, providing the Filament admin panel presentation layer over the framework-neutral core.

nodes.label: Livewire adapter tier
nodes.description: The Livewire adapter tier for the Real Estate project, a framework-specific presentation layer planned to sit on the framework-neutral core.

nodes.label: Core (domain) tier
nodes.description: The Core (domain) tier of the Real Estate project holding framework-neutral business logic that the Filament, Livewire, and API adapters present.

nodes.label: Real Estate delivery order (three phases)
nodes.rationale: Delivery is sequenced so that the core transaction chain lands first, then progression/marketing/reporting, then lettings and management — later phases depend on contracts the earlier ones establish.
nodes.description: The Real Estate delivery order defines the three-phase rollout plan for the Liberu Real Estate scope: core transaction chain first, then progression/portals, then lettings/management.

nodes.label: Delivery phase 1: core transaction chain and website feed
nodes.description: Delivery phase 1 of the Liberu Real Estate project, covering the core transaction chain and website feed capabilities.

nodes.label: Delivery phase 2: progression, portals, marketing, reporting, documents
nodes.description: Delivery phase 2 of the real estate project roadmap, covering sales progression, portals, marketing, reporting, and documents capabilities, documented in projects/real-estate/REAL-ESTATE.md.

nodes.label: Delivery phase 3: lettings, management, accounting, owner/tenant portals
nodes.description: Delivery phase 3 covers lettings, property management, accounting, and owner/tenant portals in the real estate module's three-phase delivery plan.

nodes.label: Team-scoped, authorization-aware, auditable records
nodes.rationale: All records are team-scoped, authorization-aware, auditable and subject to retention and recovery rules — a single cross-cutting invariant asserted for every capability rather than re-decided per module.
nodes.description: Team-scoped, authorization-aware, auditable records describes a core architectural property of domain records within the Liberu Real Estate scope.

nodes.label: Replaceable provider integration adapters
nodes.rationale: Provider integrations belong in replaceable adapters rather than core packages, so a third-party portal or transport can be swapped without a domain change and provider credentials never leak into the core.
nodes.description: Replaceable provider integration adapters, a documented design principle in projects/real-estate/REAL-ESTATE.md that portal integrations are independently replaceable within the Liberu Real Estate scope.

nodes.label: 'planned' as an explicit backlog marker
nodes.rationale: Rows marked planned are explicit backlog items, not claims of implementation — the table is honest about what does not exist so a reader cannot mistake a roadmap entry for a shipped package.
nodes.description: 'planned' is a documentation marker used in the Real Estate core README to flag capabilities (e.g. lettings, property management) that are on the backlog but not yet implemented.

nodes.label: Adapters stay planned until core contracts exist
nodes.rationale: Remaining API, Filament and Livewire adapters are deliberately marked planned until their matching core contracts exist, so no adapter is published against a boundary that has not been settled.
nodes.description: Documents that presentation adapters remain unimplemented until their underlying core domain contracts exist.

nodes.label: Foundation adapters vs product scope
nodes.rationale: Shared panel and interactive adapters are supplied by the foundation packages while product resources and components stay under their owning project scope, keeping product features out of the shared foundation.
