nodes.label: liberusoftware/boilerplate-scripts
nodes.rationale: Release and maintenance automation is generic and shipped as a dev dependency rather than copied per meta repository, so every Composer-based meta repo whose modules and themes live in independent GitHub repositories runs the same tooling.
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/boilerplate-scripts package holding fleet-management scripts such as scripts/fleet, measure-coverage, measure-phpstan, set-coverage-thresholds and set-phpstan-levels.

nodes.label: .liberu-meta.json meta-repository config
nodes.rationale: One copied-and-customized config carries organization, genre, repository, component paths, prefixes and extra Composer packages, so the scripts stay generic.
nodes.description: The .liberu-meta.json file, a meta-repository configuration used by the boilerplate-scripts tooling.

nodes.label: setup.sh
nodes.rationale: Performs a repeatable local or production install without destructive migrations.
nodes.description: setup.sh is a non-interactive, fail-on-error setup script from liberusoftware/boilerplate-scripts referenced in scripts/README.md.

nodes.label: update.sh
nodes.rationale: Updates dependencies and validates the project; --release 1.2.3 only commits, tags, pushes and creates the GitHub release after the checks succeed.
nodes.description: A non-interactive, fail-on-error shell script (update.sh) in scripts/ used with Packagist credentials from the environment.

nodes.label: submit-packagist.php
nodes.description: A non-interactive, fail-on-error script (submit-packagist.php) that submits or updates a package listing on Packagist using credentials from the environment.

nodes.label: scripts/fleet
nodes.rationale: Fans a command across the component repositories once those repositories are the source of truth. tag is deliberately separate and only ever acts on an explicit --only list, because a tag is what gets published while a push is recoverable.
nodes.description: scripts/fleet, the CLI tool documented in scripts/README.md that clones, runs commands across, commits, and tags the fleet of liberu-module/liberu-theme component repositories.

nodes.label: publish-components (removed)
nodes.rationale: Rsynced a monorepo into its component repositories — the opposite direction, and meaningless once those repositories are the source of truth. Replaced by fleet.
nodes.description: publish-components, a removed script documented in scripts/README.md that used to rsync the monorepo into individual package repositories, superseded by the fleet-driven publishing workflow.

nodes.label: set-coverage-thresholds
nodes.rationale: Writes each measured figure into the package's tests.yml, ratcheting only upward — a package that has lost coverage keeps its threshold and is reported rather than silently lowered.
nodes.description: A boilerplate-scripts CLI command that writes measured per-package code coverage thresholds into each repository's tests.yml workflow inputs, raising only.

nodes.label: measure-coverage
nodes.rationale: Resolves each package from nothing and runs its own suite under pcov, so the figure is evidence from a standalone resolution rather than the host's.
nodes.description: measure-coverage, a boilerplate-scripts command that measures each package's test coverage and writes results to storage/app/coverage.tsv.

nodes.label: measure-phpstan
nodes.rationale: Finds the highest level each package's src/ passes by bisection over a standalone resolution; levels are monotone, so four runs settle it instead of eleven.
nodes.description: measure-phpstan, a boilerplate-scripts command that bisects each package's PHPStan ceiling and writes results to storage/app/phpstan.tsv.

nodes.label: set-phpstan-levels
nodes.rationale: Writes each measured level into tests.yml as the reusable workflow's phpstan-level input, ratcheting only upward and preserving the existing coverage-threshold.
nodes.description: A boilerplate-scripts CLI command that writes measured per-package PHPStan levels into each repository's tests.yml workflow inputs, raising only.

nodes.label: Upward-only quality ratchet
nodes.rationale: Both coverage thresholds and PHPStan levels are per-package figures that only ever rise; a regression is reported instead of relaxing the gate.
nodes.description: The upward-only quality ratchet policy that raises coverage and PHPStan-level thresholds per package but never lowers them.

nodes.label: Non-interactive, fail-on-error commands
nodes.rationale: All commands are non-interactive and fail on errors so they can run unattended in CI.
nodes.description: A documented convention that scripts under scripts/ run non-interactively and fail fast on error, as described in scripts/README.md.

nodes.label: Packagist credentials from the environment
nodes.rationale: PACKAGIST_USERNAME and PACKAGIST_API_TOKEN are read from the environment and must never be committed; GitHub operations require an authenticated gh CLI.
nodes.description: Packagist credentials read from environment variables by scripts such as submit-packagist.php and update.sh to authenticate package publishing.

nodes.label: Component repositories are the source of truth
nodes.rationale: Modules, themes and shared tooling live in independent GitHub repositories; the meta repository is Composer output, which is what makes a monorepo-to-package sync meaningless and a fan-out runner correct.
nodes.description: States that each package's own repository, not the tracked monorepo copy, is the authoritative source of truth.

nodes.label: storage/app/coverage.tsv
nodes.description: storage/app/coverage.tsv, a tab-separated file produced by scripts/measure-coverage and consumed by scripts/set-coverage-thresholds to record each package's coverage baseline.

nodes.label: storage/app/phpstan.tsv
nodes.description: storage/app/phpstan.tsv, a tab-separated file produced by scripts/measure-phpstan recording each package's bisected PHPStan level ceiling, consumed by scripts/set-phpstan-levels.

nodes.label: per-package tests.yml workflow inputs
nodes.description: Per-package tests.yml workflow inputs, documented in scripts/README.md, the coverage-threshold and phpstan-level parameters each repository's CI workflow reads.

nodes.label: theme.json manifest
nodes.rationale: The manifest is the single declared surface for name, type, parent and asset entry points; it is the only asset entry-point index, so build inputs are derived from it rather than listed twice.
nodes.description: The theme.json manifest file format used by every theme package (base, default, dark, clear-signal, real-estate-default) to declare name, version, provider, type, parent theme, and assets.

nodes.label: Theme parent inheritance chain
nodes.rationale: A public theme declares base as its parent and resolves missing views and assets up the chain, so only the shared root has to ship every layout.
nodes.description: The theme parent inheritance chain, the mechanism by which public themes like clear-signal, dark, default, and real-estate-default declare a parent (base) and inherit its layouts and assets.

nodes.label: Theme type: shared
nodes.description: The 'shared' theme type documented in themes/base/README.md, describing the base theme's role as the shared root other themes extend.

nodes.label: Theme type: public
nodes.description: 'Theme type: public' identifica o tema default como um tema do tipo público, destinado a ser exibido a visitantes do site em vez de aos painéis administrativos.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-support
nodes.description: liberusoftware/theme-support, the package providing the theme discovery and management services used by the base, clear-signal, dark, default, and real-estate-default themes.

nodes.label: Presentation-only package boundary
nodes.rationale: A theme carries no domain behaviour — that stays in modules — and the host keeps control of theme selection and fallback, so a theme can never become a place where business rules hide.
nodes.description: The presentation-only package boundary rule stating that theme packages contain only presentation assets, not domain logic.

nodes.label: Host-controlled theme selection (config/theme.php, THEME_* env)
nodes.description: The host-controlled theme selection mechanism, documented in themes/base/UPGRADING.md, driven by config/theme.php and THEME_* environment variables.

nodes.label: Safe theme fallback
nodes.rationale: Hosts must retain a working base/default theme so that an unavailable optional asset or capability degrades instead of breaking the page.
nodes.description: The safe theme fallback rule ensuring the site renders an empty, safe state rather than erroring when a theme-dependent module is unavailable.

nodes.label: Theme accessibility baseline
nodes.rationale: Keyboard access, visible focus, semantic landmarks, readable contrast, reduced motion, zoom/reflow and system-font fallbacks are required of every theme, not optional polish.
nodes.description: Theme accessibility baseline, a documented requirement described in themes/base/README.md that applies across the base, clear-signal, dark, default, and real-estate-default themes.

nodes.label: Host Vite build of theme entry points
nodes.rationale: vite.config.js derives its inputs from themes/*/theme.json, so installing a theme is enough to get it built — and a directory rename changes the input set, requiring a rebuild.
nodes.description: The host's Vite build pipeline that compiles theme entry points into bundled CSS/JS assets under enforced size budgets.

nodes.label: Declared asset entry points (resources/css/app.css, resources/js/app.js)
nodes.description: The declared asset entry points (resources/css/app.css, resources/js/app.js) that each theme package registers so Vite can build its CSS and JS bundles.

nodes.label: No bundled third-party assets without provenance
nodes.rationale: Themes ship their own sources only; any font, image, icon, video or template added later must carry its licence and attribution.
nodes.description: 'No bundled third-party assets without provenance' é uma diretriz do README do tema base que proíbe incluir ativos de terceiros sem procedência documentada nos temas Liberu.

nodes.label: Theme testing expectations
nodes.rationale: Manifest parsing, provider registration, production asset compilation, supported host surfaces, responsive layout, keyboard navigation, contrast and fallback are all validated, and visual changes carry before/after evidence.
nodes.description: São as expectativas de teste documentadas no README do tema base para garantir que cada tema (base, clear-signal, dark, default) permaneça válido e completo.

nodes.label: Unpublished theme preview image
nodes.rationale: No maintained preview is published yet; one must be added under .github/assets/ before claiming visual-regression coverage.
nodes.description: An unpublished theme preview image, a documented gap noted as a 'planned' backlog item across the base, clear-signal, dark, and default themes.

nodes.label: Private security disclosure (security@liberusoftware.com)
nodes.rationale: Vulnerabilities must not be reported through public issues.
nodes.description: É o canal de divulgação privada de vulnerabilidades de segurança (security@liberusoftware.com) documentado no README do tema base.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/boilerplate-laravel host
nodes.description: liberusoftware/boilerplate-laravel, the host application package documented in themes/base/README.md that composes the base and public theme packages.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/real-estate-laravel host
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/real-estate-laravel host application that composes the real-estate-default theme and its modules.

nodes.label: base theme (Liberu Base)
nodes.rationale: Shared semantic tokens, accessible layout and progressive presentation primitives live at the shared root so every public theme inherits one accessible baseline.
nodes.description: The Liberu Base theme package providing shared semantic design tokens (Tailwind v4 + CSS) used as the shared root for public themes.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-base
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-base Composer package providing the shared base theme that other public themes inherit from.

nodes.label: default theme (Liberu Default)
nodes.rationale: Neutral public and portal defaults built on Liberu Base.
nodes.description: The Liberu Default theme package used as a public theme for the boilerplate host application.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-default
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-default Composer package providing the Liberu Default public theme.

nodes.label: dark theme (Liberu Dark)
nodes.rationale: Dark, reduced-glare presentation with a system fallback.
nodes.description: The Liberu Dark theme package, a public theme variant for the boilerplate host application.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-dark
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-dark Composer package providing the Liberu Dark public theme.

nodes.label: clear-signal theme (Clear Signal)
nodes.rationale: Teal signal on a quiet neutral workbench.
nodes.description: The Clear Signal Liberu theme package, a public theme with optional blog publishing and localization capabilities.

nodes.label: liberusoftware/theme-clear-signal
nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-clear-signal Composer package providing the Clear Signal public theme.

nodes.label: real-estate-default theme
nodes.rationale: Presentation only: it composes the default and base parents, owns real-estate visual identity and view composition, and never queries module tables, replaces policies or implements domain workflows.
nodes.description: The real-estate-default Liberu theme package providing the default look and feel for the real estate application.

nodes.description: The liberusoftware/theme-real-estate-default Composer package providing the real estate default public theme.

nodes.label: Optional capability: foundation.localization
nodes.description: Optional capability: foundation.localization, a documented optional feature that themes such as base, clear-signal, dark, and default may depend on.

nodes.label: Optional capability: foundation.theme-support
nodes.description: Optional foundation capability that a theme can declare it depends on for theme-support functionality.

nodes.label: Optional capability: blog.publish
nodes.description: Optional capability blog.publish, declared by the clear-signal (Clear Signal) theme in its README.

nodes.label: Declared supported host surfaces
nodes.rationale: A theme names the host surfaces it supports (application.shell, identity.auth, foundation.account, blog.index) so a host can tell before installing which screens it actually covers.
nodes.description: É a lista de superfícies do host (admin, app, público etc.) que o tema base declara suportar, conforme documentado em seu README.

nodes.label: Theme rename: liberu-base becomes base (2.0)
nodes.rationale: standards/THEMES.md derives both the repository name and the install path from one {name}, and this theme carried three different ones. A theme's name is a stable manifest surface, so making the manifest agree with the unchanged Composer package name is a major release.
nodes.description: A documented breaking change in the base theme's 2.0 upgrade guide renaming the package from liberu-base to base.

nodes.label: standards/THEMES.md
nodes.rationale: Derives repository name and install path from a single {name}, which is why three divergent names counted as a defect.
nodes.description: standards/THEMES.md, a documentation standard referenced by the base theme's UPGRADING.md guide, which covers the liberu-base to base theme rename.

nodes.label: ThemeDiscovery realpath dedupe
nodes.rationale: Discovery merges the tracked tree with Composer's installed theme packages and dedupes by realpath — so mid-wave a stale themes/liberu-base and a fresh themes/base do not dedupe and two themes appear until the stale directory is removed.
nodes.description: ThemeDiscovery realpath dedupe is the mechanism documented in themes/base/UPGRADING.md by which ThemeDiscovery deduplicates themes found both in the tracked tree and via the composer-installer by resolved realpath.

nodes.label: Child-theme relative CSS import across install dirs
nodes.rationale: A child theme importing the shared root by path crosses the install directory, so a rename of the parent directory moves the import path with it.
nodes.description: Documented issue in the base theme's UPGRADING notes about relative CSS imports breaking across different install directories in a child theme.

nodes.label: Real-estate theme extension points
nodes.rationale: Stable named slots (real-estate.properties.card/grid/search, modules.real-estate.properties.show, module-extension-points) let a theme compose views while module actions, validation, authorization, API contracts and Livewire state stay owned by their packages.
nodes.description: The customization points the real-estate-default theme exposes for extending its Livewire-rendered real estate property views.

nodes.label: Semantic design tokens (Tailwind v4 + CSS custom properties)
nodes.rationale: Components consume semantic tokens rather than hard-coded brand values, so canvas, surface, text, focus, state, typography, spacing, motion and layering can be re-themed without touching components.
nodes.description: Semantic design tokens implemented with Tailwind v4 and CSS custom properties in the real-estate-default theme, supporting light/dark and high-contrast modes.

nodes.label: Asset budgets: 80 KiB CSS / 40 KiB JS compressed
nodes.rationale: The manifest is the only asset entry-point index and generated output is not committed; the budget keeps the built theme small enough for a portal front end.
nodes.description: Documented asset budget in the real-estate-default theme README limiting compiled output to 80 KiB CSS and 40 KiB JS compressed.

nodes.label: Light/dark, high-contrast and forced-colors modes
nodes.description: Documented support in the real-estate-default theme README for light/dark, high-contrast, and forced-colors display modes via semantic design tokens.

nodes.label: LTR/RTL logical properties and translated strings
nodes.description: A design requirement that the real-estate-default theme support LTR/RTL logical CSS properties and translated strings.

nodes.label: Graceful operation without JavaScript and reduced motion
nodes.description: A design requirement that the real-estate-default theme degrade gracefully without JavaScript and honor reduced-motion preferences.

nodes.label: Empty server-rendered state when a module is absent
nodes.rationale: Missing optional modules and unavailable real-estate data render empty states rather than errors, so the theme works on a compatible non-optimized host.
nodes.description: Documented behavior of the real-estate-default theme README that it server-renders an empty state when a required module is not installed or enabled.

nodes.label: No analytics, embeds or external media
nodes.rationale: The theme carries no credentials, analytics, advertising, external embeds or privileged data; CSP, CSRF, consent and secure asset delivery remain host responsibilities, and Blade escapes output by default.
nodes.description: A design requirement that the real-estate-default theme include no third-party analytics, embeds, or external media.

nodes.label: Semantic versioning over tokens, slots, view names, entry points
nodes.rationale: Breaking changes to tokens, slots, view names or asset entry points require a major version, because those are the surfaces a consuming host builds against.
nodes.description: Documented policy in the real-estate-default theme README that semantic versioning governs the theme's design tokens, slots, view names, and entry points as its breaking-change surface.

nodes.label: Pest 5 suite and Install/Tests/Visual/Compatibility workflows
nodes.rationale: The independent repository runs its own workflows; visual evidence covers responsive CSS, reduced motion, forced colors, RTL and semantic markup, with browser screenshots deferred until the host's visual runner exists.
nodes.description: The Pest 5 test suite and CI workflows (Install/Tests/Visual/Compatibility) documented for the real-estate-default theme.

nodes.label: Deferred React/Vue/Nuxt/mobile adapters
nodes.description: Documented planned future adapters (React, Vue, Nuxt, mobile) for the real-estate-default theme that have not yet been built.

nodes.label: Do not edit installed files under themes/
nodes.rationale: Installed theme directories are Composer output; a local edit is overwritten by the next update, so selection goes through the manifest and THEME_* host configuration.
nodes.description: Aviso na documentação do tema real-estate-default alertando que os arquivos instalados em themes/ não devem ser editados diretamente, pois os repositórios de componentes são a fonte da verdade.

nodes.label: Code-level Conformance Audit
nodes.rationale: Documents where the 40-module/4-theme fleet stands against liberusoftware/documentation code-level standards. Deliberately fixes nothing -- each finding is a separate decision taken later with the measurement in hand.

nodes.label: Real Estate Legacy Parity Note
nodes.rationale: Records that the legacy 'old' branch's application classes are evidence of prior behavior, not dependencies to restore -- the modular real-estate packages and closed architecture issues are authoritative.
